utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. And good morning to you, sir. I hope you're feeling a little better. I doubt that we will detain you for long today. The affirmation you made at the beginning you ever your evidence still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Zivkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good Mr. Ajrullai. My name is Jasmina Zivkovic, and together with my colleague, Antonio Apostolski, we're the Defence of Mr. Tarculovski. In answering to the question of my learned colleague from the Prosecution and Defence, you gave us your basic information. Tell me, your basic education, you completed in Ljuboten in your native Albanian language. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And you served army in Tetovo, Veles, and Berovo. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I presume that you were trained to work with infantry weapons in the army. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, Mr. Ajrullai, you said that on the 10th of August, 2001, 8.00 a.m., you were in the your vehicle near the mosque. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was near the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Then you heard shooting and grenades from the mountains of -- to the north. You have already said that to my colleague. Do you recall how many grenades you heard in the village?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember how many.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You also, in your statement, you said that you knew that the army was in the mountains above the village of Ljuboten. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant the Macedonian army. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Of the Macedonian army, yes, this is what I was thinking. Then I presume, then, you surely knew that a few months prior to the events in Ljuboten, the Macedonian army took the positions in the mountains first, due to more frequent attacks of the territory -- of the terrorists on the village. Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Can you repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Are you an aware that, prior to the events of Ljuboten, there were terrorists attacks on the surrounding villages? Had you heard about this?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement, you explained that with your family, on the 5th -- Friday, the 10th of August to the 12th August, you were in the basement of Sulejman Zendeli. You told the Court this yesterday, and my learned colleague Residovic: You gave the answer that you only left the house from time to time, but that you did not see anything in particular. Does this mean that you could not see who was shooting and from where?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you spent the time mostly in the basement, as you said, does this mean that could you not see who was shooting and from where they were shooting towards [as interpreted] the village? Do you recall that you said yesterday ...

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm just told that the interpretation is not correct. It is not "towards the village."

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: In the village, in general, the shooting that you -- who is shooting and from where they were shooting. You said to my colleague that you left only from the basement to -- for personal needs. Do you recall saying this yesterday?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that, because you did not leave the basement other than for your personal needs, that you could not know who was shooting and from where in the village? Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. Can you repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ajrullai, in the basement of Mr. Sulejman Zendeli, how many people were there in the basement, approximately?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the accurate number; around 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And, yesterday, you said to my colleague that you don't know about the rest, but that you left the basement on occasion for personal needs. Do you recall saying this?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: The rest of the time you spent in the basement then. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You could not see from there who and from where was shooting in the village, is this correct, from the basement?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need to comment on this, if I'm allowed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On Friday, I saw where the shooting was coming from during the time I was in the basement, so I don't understand what she's asking me about. I saw the shelling coming from the north, and it was on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you comment about shelling on Saturday or Sunday? Did you see any shelling on Saturday or Sunday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only heard the noise of the shelling; whereas, on Friday, I saw them shelling from the north, and I couldn't understand why they were shelling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And the noise you heard of shelling on Saturday and Sunday, were you able to tell where that noise was coming from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the Sulon area, from the hill, there is a village there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Were you able to hear the sound of any explosions in your village on Saturday or Sunday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that helping?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ajrullai, you said that -- yesterday, you told us that on the 12th of August, on the Sunday, at 5.00 p.m., you started towards Skopje. You were stopped at a check-point, Kodra e Zajmit. Is this correct? Do you remember saying this yesterday?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: After the check, you were put in a police jeep and taken to the police station Butel. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you say that you recall that, with you on this occasion in the jeep, there were Halil Ajrullai; your uncle; Sulejman and Xhabit Zendeli; and Murtezan, who is a mentally, unstable person. Do you remember saying this?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Halil Ajrullai was not in the jeep.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: The rest, which I mentioned, were in the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question, because I'm not sure about the names you put to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You -- your brother Hazbi was not in the car?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was only myself with some other villagers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: That means that your brother Hazbi was not with you in the same vehicle, if I understand correctly?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, he was not.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, your brother, Hazbi, also says that, in the vehicle, Murtezan was with him, the person which I just mentioned earlier as a mentally unstable person. He also says that he was with him in the vehicle, but does not mention you. Can you tell us, who was with him in the jeep, you or your brother?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question? I'm not clear about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I just enumerated a list of persons. Sulejman and Xhabit Zendeli, Murtezan were you with the police jeep, on the way to the Butel police station. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sulejman was not with me. Murtezan and some other persons, whose names I don't remember, they were with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement -- in your statement, on page 4 in item 9, you say that you were with your uncle, Halil Ajrullai; Sulejman and Xhabit Zendeli, and the mentally unstable person from Ljuboten called Murtezani. You say that in your statement given to the investigators of the OTP. Do you remember all this now?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the police check-point when they beat us. They detained us there, and they maltreated us. These -- these were the persons that with me there at this point, but not in the jeep. I remember only Murtezan being in the jeep with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: In the police station Butel, was Sulejman Zendeli with you or not?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, as you said, you were taken to the police station Karpos. Yesterday, you were tell us about the paraffin test. Can we definitely establish that you know that the paraffin test shows the use of a firing weapon?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You know that this test is for this purpose. I did not say that you used such arms, but that this is a test carried out to establish whether someone has used a fire-arm or not. Do you know this?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, this witness is not an expert witness, and I believe that he cannot comment on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know the result, according to the police, of the paraffin test that was conducted on your hands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that may bring an end to that line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: After that, you were taken to the police station Bit Pazar, where you spoke to the commander. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was with some ranks, a commander or I don't know who.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. He gave you -- he allowed you to wash up and have a glass of water. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I have one more question for you, Mr. Ajrullai. Is it correct that you were, in effect, let go from the police station because you were in no connection with the UCK, and that you were not in any way part of the shooting in Ljuboten on the 12th of August? Do you know that you were let go because of this?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Am I allowed to explain it a little bit more, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they released me. After they were done with us, in the sense that they beat us up, they maltreated us. They saw that they were simply farmers, and there was no reason at all why we should be there. I'm very much surprised to this day why should the Macedonian police and army fire against civilians. This is something which I don't understand to this day. We were and are Macedonian citizens. We are born there, we will die there in Macedonia, so I don't see why. This is a mystery to me. They didn't what they wanted with us, they reduced us to that state, and then they let us free. Of course, they would let us free then. Like saying, "Oh, well, we apologise to you now." That is all I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I did not get the answer to my question. My question was: If and whether you knew that you were released because you were in no connection with the UCK, and that were in no connection with the shooting in Ljuboten. Please just tell me whether you are aware of this?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, I can. Is it correct that you were released from the police, that you did not go to gaol because you were in no connection with the UCK and in no connection with the shooting in Ljuboten. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I make a comment, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is irrelevant. There were no fighting in Ljuboten. Why should she ask me about something which is not true? They released me because I had done nothing against the state that. That is the truth, and I'm talking about myself. They beat us and they maltreated us, and then they released us. I think the culprits should be held responsible and punished.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, no more questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much Ms. Zivkovic. Ms. Regue, are there any questions in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: A few, Your Honour

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Ajrullai, yesterday, you testified, on page 13, that you saw some houses on fire on Sunday, the 12th of August. Do you know or did you find out later who set those houses on fire?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that. The Macedonian army and police did.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Were you told how they did this, how did they set the houses on fire?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to this line of questioning. The witness has given a statement to the Prosecution and explained what a -- what he saw. To my question, he also responded in an identical manner in connection with these houses on fire. The Prosecution now wants, through this witness, to introduce information -- second-hand information which are not in connection with what I asked. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Ajrullai, you were also asked -- you were told, actually, that since you had not fired any weapon, you were released from the police stations. Your brother, Hazbi Ajrullai, was -- you testified that he was with you in the basement of Sulejman Zendeli during the weekend 10 to 12 August, 2001. My question is: Did you see him holding, using any weapon during that weekend?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he never had a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Was your brother released with you on the 13th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was imprisoned.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Was -- do you know how long he was in prison?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think around four months. I can't remember the accurate dates.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. You answered that you never file any report with a committee of the Ministry of Interior established to investigate the improper conduct of the police towards Albanians. My question is: Did you know that such a committee exist?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Were you ever contacted by any member of this alleged committee?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. What is this committee you are asking me about?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If you were contacted by any member of the Ministry of Interior, of the police, after you were released from the prisons, asking you what was going on, what has happened to you.

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. They never contacted me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: You also testified that, after your experience with the police, you didn't trust the Macedonian authorities. Why you didn't trust them?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I answer? I don't have any trust because I can't understand why it happened that, from Friday, people were minding their own business, and then they were fired at, all of us. Men, women, children, we were all working. And I don't understand the conduct of the Macedonian police and the army and the courts as well. That's why I don't have any trust in them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honour. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You will be pleased to know, sir, that concludes the questions that are to be asked of you. The Chamber would thank you for coming to The Hague and for the assistance that you have given us. And you may now, of course, return to your home and your other activities. So thank you, and the court officer will show you out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you to you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And the Court officer will bring in the next witness when he returns. Thank you. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next Prosecution witness will be led by my colleague Mr. Gerard Dobbyn. Mr. Dobbyn practices criminal law in New Zealand, as well as in the United States. Matthias Neuner, who was with the Prosecution team, has moved on to the Delic trial, and so we were fortunate to have the skills of Mr. Dobbyn to assist us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much, and welcome to Mr. Dobbyn. Is that D-o-b-b-y-n?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And while we're waiting, could you indicate the name of the next witness, Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The name of the next witness is Sedat Murati.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Murati. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card that is given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Try, if you can, to forget the microphones. They often distract people. Forget those and concentrate on counsel, and I think that Mr. Dobbyn has some questions for you. He is to your right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Murati, how are you?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, do you recall giving a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on 6th October, 2004?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you recall that, on 26th April, 2007, the statement was certified by an officer of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: At that time, did you have an opportunity to read the statement in your native language?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Are you satisfied that the content of this statement is accurate and correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time, I would seek to tender the statement bearing ERN N006-4262 through N006-4275 pursuant to Rule 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P405, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And at this time, with Your Honour's permission, I will read a summary of this particular statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: "The witness, Sedat Murati, is a Macedonian citizen of Albanian ethnicity, who was 14 years old and a resident of Ljuboten in August 2001. On Friday, 10 August 2001, the witness observed the build up of police forces around Ljuboten, particularly in the area of the orthodox church and the meat factory. At the same time, gun-fire and sporadic shelling was being directed at the village. "On Sunday, 12 August, 2001, the witness heard intensive shooting and shelling commencing at approximately 8.00 a.m.. He observed a number of houses in Ljuboten suffering damage as a result of this attack. The witness left his house and went to the home of Hamit Hamiti, where he tried to provide assistance to the mortally wounded Dalip Murati. Along with others, the witness then took cover by a stream. The witness returned to his home some time after 5.00 p.m. when the shooting and shelling had stopped. "Within a few days after the attack on Ljuboten, the village leaders negotiated with the police to allow an armoured personnel carrier to enter the village to confirm that no unarmed persons were present. The witness personally observed this APC manned by police officers drive through the village." And at this time, can I please call up 65 ter number 115.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the interpreters please ask the new Prosecutor to speak slower, because there is interpretation going on in several languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are reaching the end in the fifth language of the interpretation of your comments, so you can carry on now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, do you recognise the photo that appears on the screen in front of you? There is no need to use the pen at this time.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Can you tell me, in general, what does this photograph depict?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: It depicts the village of Ljuboten and the positions of the Macedonian forces, the police and army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you identify the handwriting on the lower side of the photo?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes, it's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can we assume, from the date that is noted on this photo, that these are notations were made by you at the same time you gave your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on 6th October, 2004?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I would now like to go over the annotations that you made on the photo, starting on the right of the photo and moving to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If we could move over to the far right side of photo, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: On the far right-hand side of the photo, there is an annotation "check-point." In paragraph 10, of your witness statement, you refer to the police fortifying a check-point on a hill over the -- in the direction of Ljubanci. Is that the check-point that this notation is intended to represent?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: The next notation reads: "Hamit Hamiti shtepi." In paragraph 24 of your statement, you describe leaving your home and going to the house of Hamit Hamiti. Is that the location shown by the circle with the line linked to the words "Hamit Hamiti shtepi"?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you just remember to slow the pace a little Mr. Dobbyn?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: The next notation reads: "Sedat's house shtepi." What does that depict?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: It depicts the location where I was and from where I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: The next notation reads: "Kissa Ortodokse." In paragraph 11 of your statement, you describe seeing police moving in the direction of the orthodox church. Is the orthodox church depicted by the circle linked to the words "Kissa Ortodokse"?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes. It's that church.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: The next notation reads: "Dalip Murati shtepi." In paragraph 16 and 17 of your statement, you describe the house of Dalip Murati as being hit by grenades or shells. Is that house depicted by the circle linked to the words "Dalip Murati shtepi"?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes, that's his house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, paragraphs 23 to 25 of your statement, you describe a man you believed to be a police reservist firing a Zolja in the direction -- from the direction of the meat factory, and then finding an unexploded Zolja in the wall of the Murati house. Is this the same house you circled and labelled on the picture as "Dalip Murati shtepi"?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question. I did not quite follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Of course. In your statement, in paragraphs 23 to 25, you described an incident where you saw a man you believed to be a police reservist firing a Zolja from the direction of the meat factory. You also described then finding an unexploded Zolja in the wall of the Murati house. This house, where the unexploded Zolja was, is this the same house you have labelled as "Dalip Murati shtepi"?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: It's not marked with "Dalip Murati," but it should be marked with "Latif Latifi," where the meat factory is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And that is the location from where the man was firing the Zolja?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, on the photograph in front of you, is a that labelled "Latif Latifi Mishtore"?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise to my colleague for interrupting, but I was just wondering whether he would be kind enough to ask the witness to locate the meat factory. We're not sure we have understand which of the two houses he was referring to. We would be most grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, is the meat factory the same building you have labelled "Latif Latifi Mishtore" on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: It's the same building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: The next notation on the photograph reads: "Mirce shtepi." And in paragraphs 35 and 36, you refer to a house belonging to a Macedonian named Mirce that was set on fire. Is that the house that is indicated on this picture by the circle linked to the words "Mirce shtepi"?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters wish to indicate there is a lot of noise, and we can't really hear what is being said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, I would just -- perhaps if you sat a little bit back from the microphone. Could you move your chair back just a short distance. Can you please move your chair back just a short distance, that would assist in us being able to hear things clearer. Sorry, back further away from the microphone. The final annotation on the photograph is a short phrase beginning with the word "Kronuga." Could you please explain what that annotation represents?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat it once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: The last annotation on the photograph to the left starts with the word "Kronuga." Could you please tell us what that represents?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: This is the road along which I moved and helped the Ljuboten residents during the whole time, by distributing them food, blankets, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I would seek to tender this photograph at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P406, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And I would ask that the same photograph be kept up, so the witness can make one further annotation to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, in paragraph 17 of your statement, you describe the house of your uncle, Jakup Miftari, being shot at by police using automatic and machine guns. With the assistance of the usher, could you please locate your uncle's house on this photo?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And could you put the number 1 on the top of that mark, please, just above that mark?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Is it okay like this?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you. Where were the police shooting from when they were shooting at that house?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: From the direction of the check-point, the Macedonian check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And could you put a number 2 by that location.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I would seek to tender this photograph, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P407, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher that is all the assistance we need there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: In paragraph 11 of your statement, you describe seeing police reservists in and around Ljuboten on 10 to 12 August, 2001, dressed in camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: At this time, I would to call 65 ter number 199.16, which has been admitted as Exhibit P15 and is also photograph A on page 23 of the Prosecution's court binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, can you tell us what this is a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: This photograph shows the uniforms of the Macedonian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, since 12 August, 2001 until today, have you ever been contacted by anyone from the Macedonian police or from the Macedonian authorities and asked about what took place in Ljuboten on 10 to 12 August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I have no further questions at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Dobbyn. Mr. Mettraux

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Murati. My name is Guenael Mettraux, and together with my colleague Edina Residovic, I'm representing Mr. Boskoski. In your statement, you explained that, on the 12th of August 2001, the shooting in and around the village started at around 8.00 in the morning. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you also recall saying that, shortly thereafter, shelling started in and around the village. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: It wasn't immediately after that, but several hours later.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I will rephrase the question to clarify it. Can you recall at around what time that morning you heard the first shelling landing in or around the village of Ljuboten? Can you recall the time, approximately?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: At around 3.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, sir, so that -- go ahead.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Excuse me. I mean, I'm talking about Friday, the 10th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, that was my mistake, Mr. Murati. I would like to bring you to the Sunday, the 12th of August. Can we focus on the Sunday?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: [In English] Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So can you recall at around what time the shooting started on Sunday, the 12th. Was it around 8.00?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, around 8.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall, approximately, how long after the first sound of shooting you heard the first sound of shelling on that day?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: On that day, I was asleep; and at around 8.00, the shooting started from automatic weapons, and then shelling followed immediately after.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And is that correct that, at the time when the shell started, you had taken cover inside your house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, I was already inside the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that you only came out of your house that morning at around 10.00 or 11.00. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, can you tell the Chamber how long, approximately, or at what time, approximately, you first went out of your house that morning.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: It was 12.00. The shooting ceased and we took this opportunity to leave the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So is it correct that, between around 8.00, when you were woken up, and 12.00 you remained in your house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that while you were in your house, between 8.00 and 12:00 on the 12th of August, you heard three shell landing on or around the houses of Dalip Murati. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And your evidence is that you simply heard those shells, but you didn't see their impact at the time when they landed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes. When they were fired, I went back inside the house; and when it ceased, then I went out.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that those were -- the shells that you heard landing on or around the property of Dalip Murati were the first three shells that you heard that morning, or shell impact. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that you were later told by fellow villagers that Mr. Murati had been injured by the first of those three shells. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I was not told by the villagers. This is what I saw myself. Having left the house, we were close to Hamit Hamiti's house where Dalip Murati's house is as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And one of your fellow villagers told you that the shell that had injured Mr. Dalip Murati was the first of the three shells that you had heard. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll assist you, Mr. Murati. I'd like to read a passage of your statement at paragraph 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is Exhibit P405, and if I may ask the registry to go to the fourth page of that statement at paragraph 16, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please enlarge it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, I will also -- I'll ask you to focus on paragraph 16. That's the last paragraph on the Albanian version and the first one on the English version. I'll read a sentence to you from that paragraph. It says this: "I heard a big explosion at Dalip Murati's house. All together, there were three impacts of grenades/shells on the compound of Dalip Murati. The first hit the yard and killed Dalip Murati." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Paragraph 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps we'll need to turn to the next page in the Albanian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you see the sentence, Mr. Murati? This would be the third and fourth sentence in that paragraph. I will read it to you once again. It says this: "I heard a big explosion at Dalip Murati's house. All together, there were three impacts of grenades/shells on the compound of Dalip Murati. The first hit the yard and killed Dalip Murati." Can you see that in your statement?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that you were given that information by fellow villagers?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No. Dalip Murati himself told me and his son, because I helped him when we left.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We'll come to that in a minute, Mr. Murati. Is that correct that from your house, you were not in a position to locate the position from which the shells had been fired at the house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Certainly. Is that correct that from the inside of the house, where you were between 8.00 and 12.00 that morning, you were not able to assess where the shells had been coming from, where they had been fired from. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No. I could see where they were coming from.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you could see that from the inside of your house?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes. I could see that from the balcony.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And where did the shells came from?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: One came from the side of the Macedonian roadblocks, which were in the direction of Latif Latifi's butcher shop; whereas, the third one came from the person I saw firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Wasn't it your evidence, sir, in your statement, that you said that, prior to the shelling, you had gone back into the house?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I was telling you about the third shell -- third day, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. And wasn't it your evidence, sir, that prior to the start of the shelling on the 12th, you had gone back inside the house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Certainly. Is it correct that it was your evidence, and it is the case, that you have indicated that on the 12th, the Sunday, you had gone back inside the house prior to the shelling starting. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You have indicated earlier that you had remained inside the house from 8.00 until 12.00, is that correct, on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I -- it is true that I stayed inside the house, but it is not that I was confined to a single room. I could go out in the balcony; and from there, I could see what was going on, or sometimes I watched from the window which is in the toilet, and also, as I said, from the balcony.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that correct that you told the Prosecution in your statement that you had remained in the bathroom during that time?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: But not all the time. I stayed there for a while. Most of the time, I stayed in the bathroom, because from there I could see them in the direction of the Macedonian check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that correct that you have indicated that you stayed there until 10.00, when you came out for the first time, and that the only observation that you could make were from a small window from the bath -- the bathroom?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Certainly. Is that correct that, in your statement, you indicated to the Prosecution that you had remained at all times in the bathroom, from which you could make certain observation from a small window. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes, but this doesn't mean that I stayed there all the time. I stayed in the bathroom most of the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that correct that the only time that you've indicated to the Prosecution when you went outside is, approximately, two hours after the shelling on Dalip Murati's compound at the time when you said you saw an individual carrying a Zolja. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. Is that correct that, in your statement to the Prosecution, the only occasion that you've indicated when you went out of your house was after the shelling on Mr. Murati's, Dalip Murati's house, had already occurred and an a time when you said you saw an individual carrying a Zolja. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct also that you told the Prosecution that you only heard the explosion of the grenades or shells that landed at Dalip Murati's house, but that you never exclaimed to witness the explosion. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honour, in fairness to the witness, he doesn't have his statement in front him, and I believe that is not what in stated in the statement, I believe. What it does say which should be put to him, which is: "I have only seen the second and third impact." If it assists, this is the last sentence in paragraph 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown paragraph 16, again, the last sentence. I think, in the Albanian version, it would start on the previous page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, is that your evidence -- well, I'm going to ask you another way. Can you identify the location, once again, where you said you saw the first shell being fired?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes. You mean to show it on a photo or in words?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you could show us the location, please. The location.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: In the direction of Latif Latifi's butcher's shop, but on the upper side.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness to stay a little bit away from the microphones please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, you're being asked, once again, if you could pull back a tiny bit from the microphone. Thank you very much. So, Mr. Murati, if evidence was begin in this courtroom that the fire had come not from -- towards the butcher's shop, but from the eastern part of the village, you would take issue with that suggestion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if suggestion was made that -- well, let me ask you this perhaps: Were you able to identify the individuals who had fired the first three shells on that day?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you're not in a position to say whether the individuals who fired those shells were members of the army, members of the police, or members of the NLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, that doesn't mean that I couldn't tell, because they came from the place where the Macedonian check-point were stationed, but I can't say precisely who it was that fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But if someone -- if a witness were to give evidence to the effect that those shells had been fired by the NLA, you could not take issue with that proposition. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. If a witness in this courtroom were to suggest that the first three shells, which had been sent on to the village, had come from NLA position, you would not be, yourself, in a position to contradict this evidence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I would have contradicted that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you have indicated, a moment ago, that you were not in a position to identify the individuals who fired those shells. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I couldn't identify the -- an individual from a distance of two, 300 metres away because that individual might have taken up a position in a place I couldn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll just refer to the transcript of Mr. Bolton, on the 7th of June, 2007. It's at page 1671 and 1685, and it is Exhibit 1D24.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, do you know a fellow villager named Suat Saliu? Are you familiar with that person?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is he an acquaintance of yours?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know that he was a member of the NLA at the time?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is 1D507. It has an ERN of 1D00-4667 in the English and 1D00-4674 in the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, there is no Albanian version, unfortunately, but I think you can read both English and Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I may ask the registry to turn to the second page, please, that would be paragraph 2 of this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would just like to bring your attention to the first sentence after that paragraph, Mr. Murati. Mr. Saliu told the following to the Prosecutor: "I joined the NLA in June 2001 and, initially, served with the 113th Brigade." Can you see that.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: You mean paragraph 1?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No, paragraph 2, please. Perhaps, I should ask you this,

utterances.speaker: MR. MURATI
utterances.text: Can you read the Macedonian version?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can draw your attention to the first sentence in that statement, it says: "I joined the NLA in June 2001 and, initially, served with the 113th Brigade." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you will agree that Mr. Saliu was, in fact, a member of the NLA at the time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if we can turn to the fourth page of that statement and focus on paragraph 9, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That would be ERN 4670 in the English version, and ERN 4677 in the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, I'm going to show you another paragraph of the statement of your fellow villager, Mr. Saliu.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if it could be enlarged a little bit for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: At paragraph 9 of the statement, Mr. Murati, Mr. Saliu was being asked about the events of the 12th of August, 2001 in the village of Ljuboten, and this is what he had to say: "As Macedonian forces were about to enter the village, Hoxha and Limaj ordered to open mortar fire. They obviously discussed the situation with Bushi, with whom they were in contact on mobile phone. About six or seven mortars sounds were fired. Our mortars targeted the army positions. "I think that five rounds missed the targets, while two hit the army positions. Macedonian security forces were beating the villagers of Ljuboten; and after the mortar sounds impacted, Macedonian security forces started to withdraw from the village. Some mortars were fired towards the Macedonian check-point close to the orthodox church in Ljuboten." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then Mr. Saliu adds the following: "To my knowledge, they exploded on that compound on the Macedonian part of Ljuboten, close to the so-called Chinese wall, which surrounds the house of Brace, where Ljube Boskoski, the former Minister of the Interior, was shown on TV. To my knowledge, they did not cause any damage or injuries among the Macedonian forces or villagers."

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Can I answer your question now?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps can you answer this question: Do you have any reason to take issue with the veracity of Mr. Saliu's evidence; namely, that the NLA fired a number of mortars onto the village on that day?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: This is not true. I don't know what Mr. Saliu has said here, but this has got nothing to do with the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you have any reason to challenge the veracity of Mr. Saliu's statements that some of those mortars, in any case, were fired in the proximity of your house near the orthodox church?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: This statement is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, during the weekends -- the weekend of the 10 to the 12 August, 2001, had you been monitoring the presence of NLA fighters in the village? Did you keep tab of any NLA fighters in the village?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No. I was in school during that time, and I wasn't interested in such affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise. This is my mistake, again, Mr. Murati. I was simply asking about the weekend in question, the weekend of the 10, 11, and 12th of August. I'm asking this. Perhaps, I should be clear. Did you -- well, first, did you notice the presence of any NLA fighters in the village?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you keep tab of anyone, whom you know to be a NLA fighter, about his or her presence in the village during that weekend?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No. I was simply a 14-year-old child who goes to school and who is interested in nothing else other than school.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that you knew that the village of Ljuboten was fertile ground for recruitment of NLA soldiers. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know that a number of young men from the village had been joining the ranks of the NLA during that period or prior to these events. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know, perhaps, that several members of the Murati family were members of the NLA at that time. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know, perhaps, who Rasim Murati is?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is he a relative of yours?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is he a relative of Dalip Murati?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is he from the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know who Faik Murati is?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is he a relative of yours?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what family relationship do you have to Faik Murati?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: He is the son of my uncle. He is my cousin.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could you say which uncle that would be, if you have more than one?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I'm not so certain. Are you asking me about Faik Murati?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. If you could just tell me the name of the father of Faik, Is it Jakup?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: This is it another Faik, whose last name is not Murati.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could you give me the name of the father of Faik Murati?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: There are many Faiks. I don't know any Faik Murati. The Faik I have in mind is another Faik.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it Faik Miftari?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And his father would be your uncle, Jakup. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will adjourn now for the first break. There is another matter I must attend to in the break, and it may mean that we are a little late in returning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, before the break, I was asking you about a number of villagers from Ljuboten. I would like to ask you about a few more. Do you know a person called Faredin Murati? I think, this time, I will have to ask to you move a bit closer to the microphone. Your answer was not picked up, or speak up a little bit, please.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is he a fellow villager from Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is he a relative of yours?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you say what family relationship you have with Faredin?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: My uncle's side from mother's side.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is he a cousin of yours?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know a person called Shefket Murati?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is he a fellow villager from Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is he a relative of yours?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes. When you say "villager from Ljuboten," it is true. He is from Ljuboten; but, at that time, he did not live in the village, so I wouldn't call him a fellow villager.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know where he was at that time?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes. He was working and living in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that correct that he was, in fact, a member of the NLA at the time?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, that I don't know. He was in Kosovo, as I said, and I didn't see him at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We'll come back to that in a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But with the registry's assistance, if we could see picture which is now I think P407.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, this is the same picture that was shown to you earlier by the Prosecutor upon which you made a number of markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll ask the registry to focus, if possible, on the area that has a number of circles marked already. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, on the picture in front of you, are you able to see the house of Rasim Murati, or is it outside of the framework of this picture?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: It's outside the framework.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: How about the house of Faik? Can you see it on this picture?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes. It is marked with number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll ask the --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, for the record, this is a house on the right of a circle noted, marked as "Sedat's house," with a number 1 on the top of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What about the house of Faredin, can you see it on this picture?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Farid [phoen]? [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Faredin.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Faredin's, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What about the house of Shefket?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Shefket did not have a house in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We can take the picture off the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Coming back to the four persons I named - Rasim, Faredin, Faik, and Shefket - were you aware at the time of this event they were members of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if the registry could, once again, show what is 1D507, which is the statement of Suat Saliu at paragraph 7, that would be page 3 in the English and also page 3 in the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, I'd like to draw your attention to a particular section of this paragraph. It start with the words "There were about 27 young men." Can you see that in the Macedonian version?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Which number did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Paragraph 7. That's the one at the bottom of the page. And the sentence, in the English, in any case, starts with the words: "There were about 27 young men." Can you see that, and there follow as list of names?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Give me some time to look at this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the paragraph be enlarged some more, if that is feasible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're moving it very fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps, with the usher's assistance, I can give Mr. Murati a paper copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There is the fourth sentence in the paragraph. I'll read it out to you, and I'll ask you if you can find it in the Macedonian. It says this: "There were about 27 young men from Ljuboten with the 114th Brigade. I remember the names of some of them. They are Riza Jonuzi, Islam Zendeli, Rasim Murati, Arsim Elezi, Faredin Murati, Faik Murati, Shefajet Bajrami, Besim Murtezani, Jetulla Arifi, Bekri Ajdini, Orhan Bajrami, Shefket Murati, Refedin Selimi, Suat Saliu, and Rafiz Bajrami." Sir, you have no reason to challenge the accuracy and truth of this statement of Mr. Saliu about the membership of the NLA, is that correct, in relation to these particular individuals?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I cannot comment on Suat Saliu's words.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, is it correct that your cousin, Faik, was in charge of the logistic for the NLA in the village of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I would just like to clarify here. I know questions have been asked about Faik Murati. I believe that the witness, when he was answering questions earlier on when asked about that, was in fact talking about someone by the name of "Faik Miftari," and said there were several people in the village by the name of "Faik Murati," who he did not really know about. So I think we need to clarify exactly who is being asked about and who the witness knows about.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will clarify, Your Honour, but I think the transcript says that there was no Faik Murati. I believe the evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I will ask about Mr. Faik Miftari, in any case, to clarify the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, were you aware that Faik Miftari, your cousin, was or wasn't, or if Mr. Faik Miftari was a member of the NLA. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, that's not true. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't it the case that Faik, in fact, fought for the UCK first in Kosovo and then in Tetovo? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know a person by the name of Zecir Murati?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is he a relative of yours?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Excuse me, I understand that you say Zecir Murati, but there are two Zecirs with the same last name, so I don't know which one you are referring to. Could you tell me their age or something like that that would identify who you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I think the Court and myself will be dependent on you to tell us that. Could you tell us whether, first, both of the Zecir Murati were relative of yours, or one of them?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Both of them are my cousins. One is on my mother's side, and the other on my father's side.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did both of them reside in the village of Ljuboten at the time, in August of 2001, or did one of them?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: One of them resided in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And -- yes.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: As for the other one, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware that one of the -- one of your two cousins, Zecir, was a member of the NLA at the time?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But if your village leader, Mr. Salievski, were to say so to the Office of the Prosecutor, you would have no reason to take issue with this statement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Could you please ask me a more clearer question, because I don't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will ask it differently. Is it possible that perhaps one of your cousin, Zecir, was a member of the NLA without you being aware of that fact. Is it possible?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Everything is possible; but if I don't know about something as a fact, I cannot confirm it or deny it. I cannot say anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Murati, that your father, Rahim, spent sometime in prison?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Repeat your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that your father, Rahim, was detained, was in prison for some time.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Which time-period are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In 1999 and the year 2000.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And he was arrested because weapons, an automatic gun and hand-grenades, were found in your house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you tell this Chamber why your father was imprisoned in 1999 and 2000?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: My father was imprisoned for something that was not related to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you tell us what that was, sir.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: During that time, my brother and a cousin, my aunt's son, that is, had bought something and put it in the house without the knowledge of my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And those were weapons and ammunitions and hand-grenades. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. But can you please tell me why you're asking me these questions when they have nothing to do with what we are discussing today? This happened before the war, and I'm not here to testify about what had happened to my father and what is not related to what we're discussing today.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I just ask you one more question about this. Could you tell the Chamber what were those items which were brought into your house without the knowledge of your father, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I don't feel very well. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, should we perhaps take a short break?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need some time because you mentioned my father, and my father has died.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn for quarter of an hour. --- Break taken at 11.32 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we can continue now, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, we've been informed at the break about the recent passing away of your father, and we would like to express our condolences. I have one more -- or one last question about this issue, if can you answer it. Are you able to say what item were found in your house which led to the detention of your father?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I really don't know why you're interested so much in this, when it has nothing to do with what we're talking today. It can lead to a long debate.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, are you perhaps simply able to --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I think there's been a typo at --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps, you can assist us simply be telling us whether you have knowledge of the item in question or not, simply that?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about this. I was not at home when this happened. This is all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. You will recall, earlier today, you indicated to me that you had talk with Dalip Murati. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'm still talking of the 12th of August, and you've indicated that Mr. Murati told you that he had been injured by the first shell that landed on to his property. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I suppose that if another villager, who testified before this Tribunal, suggested that Mr. Murati had been injured not on the 12th but on Saturday, the 11th, you would take issue with that evidence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you would not agree -- I'll make it clear, perhaps, for the record. You would not agree with the suggestion that Mr. Dalip Murati was, in fact, injured on Saturday, the 11th.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply for the record, this is evidence of M-92, and his statement was admitted as P215, paragraph 5 to 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You will recall I asked you earlier where you were during the hours of 8.00 to 12.00 on the 12th of August; and, at first, you told me you were inside the house. Do you recall? It was at page 22. Do you recall telling me that?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then a little later, you said, at some stage, you had gone on to the balcony. That's at page 25. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Make it clearer, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. Do you recall that a few moments after you had said that you were in your house, you said that you had made a number of observations from the balcony of your house. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you also recall being asked, by the Prosecution during your interview of the 6th of October, 2004, where you had been during these four hours, between 8.00 and 12.00? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I already told you that I was at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps, with the assistance of the registry, I'd like to show the witness, once again, his statement. That is P405, and it would be at page 4 of the statement, paragraph 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, that would be the last paragraph on this page. That's page 5 of this statement in the Albanian version. I'll just read out what you are recorded to have said to the Prosecution: "We spent four hours at our place. During this time, I monitored quite good from the first floor inside the bathroom. From that place, I have had a very good view of the area through a very small window. I can see from my house parts of the location of the orthodox church. I have a full sight over the butcher factory." Do you recall saying that to the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that was correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that this window in the bathroom faces south-east in the direction of the church and Latif Latifi's house, as a butcher shop. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that, from this window, you can't see the location which you've marked as being the check-point of the Macedonian forces?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No. You can see the check-point as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you would have to put your head outside the window. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No. There are two small windows in my bathroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, sir, that have you never indicated to the Prosecution that you made any observation from a balcony in your house? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. I've mentioned that. It's in the 21st paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I will perhaps re-read the paragraph to you. It says this: "We spent four hours at our place. During this time, I monitored quite good from the first floor inside the bathroom. From that place, I have had a very good view of the area through a very small window. I can see from my house parts of the location of the orthodox church. I have a full sight over the butcher factory." You will agree that there is no mention of a balcony and no mention of a second window. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Excuse me, but I think it is somewhere in this paragraph, or maybe in another paragraph. It should be mentioned somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that --

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I think it's when it mentions a monitoring from the window. I've said that have I been most of the time in the bathroom, which means that I spent quite a little time on the balcony, because there is no shelter in the balcony. You're quite exposed there. While there, I thought they might detect me, and that's why I went to the bathroom where I couldn't be seen. I've said these things, and they refer to something that I've done for quite some time [as interpreted]. Maybe that's why it has not been mentioned in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that, in 2001, you were a 14-year-old?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Line 4, in page 46, should read "for quite short time."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm now 20, 21, and maybe can you calculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
