utterances.text: But is that correct that, at the time, you had done no military service of any kind?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you knew, however, that the police would sometimes where blue uniforms and sometimes camouflage uniforms. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Certainly. Were you aware that the Macedonian police sometimes wore blue uniforms? Did you know that at the time?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Well, we came across policemen on the roads, on check-points. We've seen them on TV, so it's quite normal for a person to know how the police looks like in his country. This is quite usual. Everyone can know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And those police officers, which you would see at times, some of them would wear a blue uniform. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, not blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps, I'll ask you to go again to your statement, which I think is still on your screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll ask the registry to turn to page 3, and to focus, please, on paragraph 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll just read the passage to you, sir. You were being asked to describe your observation at the time, and this is what you said: "Some of them wearing masks. Being asked for the police, I say these people were wearing blue uniforms." Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, not blue. Only the colour mentioned here is in the correct. I said black T-shirts. Here it says "blue."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that police officers would sometimes where camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes, the ones we saw in the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And those are identical to those worn by the members of the army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: The army wore same uniforms as those on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that you've indicated to the Prosecutor that you did not see any patches or insignias on the individuals whom you saw in the village on the 12th of August. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You will recall that, in your statement to the Prosecution and earlier today, you've indicated seeing a man who carried what you believe to be a shoulder-propelled device, which you called a "Zolja." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you remember what time it was, approximately, when you saw that person?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't know the exact time, but it was around 10.00, about this time. At that moment, I was on the balcony at the corner of the house and I sort of stepped outside, putting myself in danger. I heard shouting coming from the other side of the village, from the residents; and, at that time, I saw this person. He was wearing a black T-shirt and military trousers. There was another person with him. I only saw his hands. And this person in question, I saw taking the Zolja from his hands. And at this time, I think they detected my presence, and they started to fire in my direction, so I sheltered in the house. When the shooting ended, I went out in the balcony as well; and, at that moment, I saw that Dalip Murati's house was on fire, and that's when I was sure that they were shooting in the direction of Dalip Murati's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall saying that the man whom you saw shooting, or carrying a Zolja, rather, was wearing a mask? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Was he also wearing something on his head? A hat, a helmet?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall how long you saw that person, for how long?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: For ten to 20 seconds, I would say, a very short time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And was he moving around while you were observing him?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No. He was getting ready to fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that, from the distance and from your observation, you could not tell whether that person was a member of the police or a member of the army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I could identify him only by his trousers, because they were the same as the pattern we saw on the photograph, but I didn't see any insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've explained, I think, that as you saw this person you returned to your house and into the basement of your house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall how long you spent in the basement prior to getting out again?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Until the shooting ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've indicated that you believed it was around 12.00. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could you indicate around what time you believe you came out of the basement of your house?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I don't understand what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, you've indicated that you, from, you said, the balcony of your house, you went back into the house and into the basement, where you stayed until the fire stopped. And I'm asking: Can you recall, approximately, what time that was when the shelling stopped and when you came out of the house; or, in any case, outside of the basement?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I didn't say "the shots," but I say "the shot." I meant the shot that I heard at that moment, which lasted at most ten seconds; and then after that, I immediately went up to the balcony.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And how long did you stay on this balcony?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: For about ten minutes. With some people from my family, we were watching the house of Dalip Murati being burned and cowshed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you hear any shelling after that time in the village?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall how many shells, approximately, fell on the village after that time?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I apologise, but it's really impossible to count or to be able to say how many shells, you know, when you keep hearing constant shelling. So I can't give you an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's fair enough?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we can move in private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, you will recall that, in your statement to the Prosecution, you explained that a number of villagers left Ljuboten on Monday, the 13th of August. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in fact, you described that, within two hour's window, the majority of the remaining citizens left. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in fact, a lot of the villagers remained outside of Ljuboten for two weeks, and for some of them for longer periods of time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Certainly. You've indicated, in your statement, and perhaps I should -- I will read it to you. It is paragraph 34 and 35 of the your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if it could be brought up for Mr. Murati's benefit. Yes. This would be paragraphs 34 and 35 at page 6, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll just ask you the question about the relevancy. You said that: "On the next morning," that's paragraph 34, "Monday, 13 August 2001, one of my relatives, cousin Latif Latifi, who is the owner of the butcher shop, came to pick up, on Monday, his daughter, and this was at a time when, in a two-hour period, a majority of the Ljuboten villagers left again the village." Can you recall saying that to the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then, if I can draw your attention to the next paragraph, paragraph 35, you say this --

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I don't see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you see it now?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: [In English] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That would be the paragraph at the bottom of the --

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, now yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You indicated, in your statement, that: "During this period of two weeks, the village was nearly empty. Only some individuals stayed." And you said: "Actually two groups." My question is: Can you recall now which two groups remained in the village during those two weeks?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: They were ordinary people who stayed at home because they had livestock to take care of, and they just guarded their own homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this may be an impossible question, Mr. Murati, in which case you will tell me so, but can you recall particularly which individuals remained in the village?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I cannot say names here because I think they are individuals that do not matter in this story; maybe 20, 25 persons all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That was an impossible question on my part, so I'll move on to something else. Do you recall telling the Prosecutor that you remembered one occasion after the events when an APC came back into the village. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's at paragraph 38, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I remember. It was a couple of weeks after, I don't remember how many weeks, and I was assured by the chairman of the village - his name was mentioned earlier on here - that the police wanted to find out whether there were KLA members. That's why they entered the village with their armoured cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the leader of the village whom you refer to would be Kenan Salievski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did he tell you that personally?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, not me personally, but some of us called him.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall now who told you about this?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No. I cannot recall who told me this, but we all learned that an armoured car was going do coming with Macedonian police to check the village. And we came -- went out, ten or 15 persons, to wait for them to come. We talked to the police, asking them why all this happened. There were four persons, and that is all.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in your statement, you indicate that one of the men accompanying this APC, you believed him to be the same man who had carried the Zolja on the 12th of August. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's the same man that you saw for only a few seconds, from 50 metres wearing a mask. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I didn't say that it is it exactly the same person, but that I believe he was the same person, because he had the same height, the same hair, the same face, the same body-build.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Was he wearing a mask at that time also?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes. He had a mask from the nose and was tied behind, but it didn't cover the entire face. I could see his hair; and through the hair, I thought that it might be the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that you also believed to have seen -- or perhaps I should ask you differently. In your statement, you've indicated that you remembered a machine-gun fixed on the top of the APC. Is that still your evidence today? Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes. There was an armoured car, APC, and there was a machine-gun on top of it. There was also a soldier next to the machine-gun ready to fire. There were four or five persons on top of it, and they were wearing the same mask. I saw another person wearing the same mask as that of the person who was firing that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So, if I were to put to you that no such vehicles, APC with guns mounted on top, were present in the Cair-Ljubanci-Ljuboten area up until the end of 2001, you would disagree with me. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I would disagree with you, because the same APCs were at police check-points, in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the driver of the APC, the person who drove the APC, one of the drivers of the APC at the time were to say that, during that period, there was only one APC in the area at that time and that that particular APC had no gun mounted on top, you would take issue with his evidence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the transcript, this is the evidence of M-37 unchallenged by the Prosecution. It is at 825, 826.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if another Prosecution witness, sir, had indicated that he saw the APC around the village on the 12th of August, and, again, indicated that there was only one such vehicle at the time and that this vehicle had no gun mounted on top, you would take issue with that evidence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: It's a rather long question. Could you please be so kind as to rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I thought that were not addressing me, and I didn't concentrate on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: My apologies. If another witness were to tell before this Tribunal that at the time and in the area, there was only one APC and that this APC had no gun mounted on top, you would take issue with the evidence of that person, just as you ask with the previous person. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I would take issues, yes. Maybe he has seen someone else. But if is he talking about this event happening on the same day, I would take issue with that, because I cannot say something that did not happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, just fort transcript, this is, again, evidence of -- well, this is the evidence of M-33, again, unchallenged by the Prosecution at 1432, and also perhaps the evidence of Witness Despodov of the 26th of June, 2007, at page 25 -- 2656, and, again, not challenged on this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, I'm very grateful for your patience. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Zivkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation], Mr. Murati, hello, my name is Jasmina Zivkovic; and together with my colleague Antonio Apostolski, we represent and defend Mr. Johan Tarculovski. Mr. Murati, you were born and you lived in the village of Ljuboten all your life. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You completed elementary school, I guess, over there?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And you graduated in your native tongue, Albanian language?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, in your statement, you have indicated that throughout these events from the 10th until the 12th of August, 2001, in Ljuboten, you were there together with your family. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: The voice comes very loud to me, and I can't concentrate.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Is this better?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Maybe he means the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Is it my voice or the voice of the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: The interpreters. Both voices get mixed up. You are speaking, she's interpreting, so it gets mixed up in my ears.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Is it any better now?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes. Now, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, during the -- before the events in Ljuboten, previously you did not have any trouble with the Macedonian population in Ljuboten. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: You mean before the war?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, we didn't. But I was simply 14 years old, and I didn't have anything to do with any of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that, on Friday, August 10th, 2001, there were shootings from time to time which started at 4.00. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that if someone would state before this Court that on Friday the shooting started earlier in the morning, this would be incorrect?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: The voice comes again very loud. Can you please do something about it?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it would help, strangely enough, Ms. Zivkovic, if you could keep your voice quieter. The witness is hearing your voice without amplification and is hearing the interpreter through his earphones, and the two, I think, are clashing. So if you could try to be quieter. It's rare that I ask this in this courtroom. If you could try, it may help the witness to hear the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you manage to hear my question, or you would like me to repeat it? Does this mean that if someone would testify before this Court that the shootings on Friday, on 10th of August, started earlier in the morning, this would be incorrect?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: It is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Also, in your statement, you have indicated that you saw a helicopter flying above the location where, on Friday morning, a mine exploded. Do you recall saying this?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall whether it was an army or a police chopper?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Army chopper. It's a military helicopter.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You probably heard that eight people died and the same number of Macedonian soldiers were injured.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And you know that this was a mine that was laid down by the members of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Before these events, you noticed that, around the village of Ljuboten, check-points have been established; and in the hills above the village, the military was positioning itself. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And this was for the reason that, prior to this mine incident, there were often attacks by the terrorist on the village, on the surrounding villages. Did you hear about this?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Is it possible that, bearing in mind that you were only 14 years old, probably you couldn't know this at that time, since you said today that at that time you were interested only in your school?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: On Friday, August 10th, you also stated that you saw policemen in the village, and that there were around ten or 15 of them. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Can you please indicate to me where I said this?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 11 on the third page. Do you recall that you have indicated that some of them were wearing regular blue uniforms and some of them were reservists?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I cannot answer to both questions at the same time. Can you please split them up.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Then let this be the first question: Do you recall saying that you saw some of the policemen in regular police uniforms and some of them in the reservists uniforms. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And you said then that you saw ten to 15 policemen, in total.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On Sunday, August 12th, the shooting in the village started after 8.00 a.m. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: At 8.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: To my learned colleague from the Defence counsel, you told him that you observed the overall situation through the window in the toilet, in the bathroom. And also you have indicated, in your statement, that, according to your opinion, the Macedonian police never tried, nor dared to move in the direction towards south, because this was -- this was the area beneath below your house; and, in such case, they would not have a place to hide. Do you recall saying this?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I don't recall to have said this. Can you please show me where?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 22, on page number 4.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Can you please enlarge it a little bit? Yes, but I meant this for Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, very well. I'm talking about Sunday as well. This means that there were terrorists in the village.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: We should clarify this. I declared this: That when the police headed towards the other side of the village, first, they started in the morning on our side of the village; but thinking that it was an open field and there were no Macedonian families there, the police were afraid. They didn't have any support coming to them from the Macedonians, and the field was completely open. And that's why they headed towards the other side of the village, because there were Macedonian check-points close -- closer to that side, and they felt more secure there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I understood the first time as well, but you still did not answer from whom the Macedonian police is supposed to hide. From the Albanians who lived there? From the terrorists? Can you explain this, please, and why would they need any cover?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. What do you mean? I really don't get it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Earlier, you explained that the area below your house is an open space, and you thought that the Macedonian police did not go in this direction because there was no cover. My question is: What kind of cover? Cover from what?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I think that they must have supposed that maybe someone might fire at them. That's why I said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And as you indicated, in the afternoon, you departed towards the stream with the rest of them; and, at that time, there was no shooting by the Macedonian police and the army as well?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Could you please speak up a little bit? I mean the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: So, at the time when you came to that stream, at that time, there was no shooting going on by the Macedonian police.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: You mean when I went to the stream with Hamit [as interpreted] Hamiti?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No. There were shootings throughout the time until 7.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And, regardless of that shooting, several times you were going back, as you indicated in your statement, for certainly supplies and blankets to the house of Cermiti [phoen] and back to the stream, in between the shooting.

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, in your statement, you have indicated that -- in paragraph 33, that you stayed around the stream until it started to get dark after 1700 hours. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Can I have a look at it, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the registry can please show the statement, P405, 33rd paragraph on page 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see paragraph 33, right in the middle in the version on Albanian?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall saying this now, when you can see it?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that in Ljuboten, in August, it is getting dark at 5.00 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: I mentioned 1700 hours, but that doesn't mean that that was the precise time. I just pointed out an approximate time. I said until it got darker. Maybe it was a little bit later.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't have any more questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Zivkovic. Mr. Dobbyn, is there any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: There will just be a few questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, you were asked several questions by my learned colleague about the shelling of Dalip Murati's house. And, at one point, my learned colleague read to you a paragraph from Suat Saliu's statement, and this was paragraph 9 of the statement, which is Defence 65 ter number 1D507. That should be coming up on your screen in a moment, Mr. Murati.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And could we focus in on paragraph 9, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This one is in English, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: There is an Albanian version also coming up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have only English and Macedonian of this document, not Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I'll read to new English, and it will be translated into Albanian, Mr. Murati. I'm starting from, approximately, the middle of the paragraph, and it states that: "Some mortars were fired towards the Macedonian check-point close to the orthodox church in Ljuboten. To my knowledge, they exploded on dead ground in the Macedonian part of Ljuboten close to the so-called Chinese wall, which surrounds the house of Brace where Ljube Boskoski, the former Minister of the Interior, was shown on TV. To my knowledge, they did not cause any damage or injuries among the Macedonian forces or villagers." Has that been interpreted for you, Mr. Murati?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now could I ask you: Is Dalip Murati's house in the Macedonian part of the village?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Are there any other houses around Dalip Murati's house?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes. His houses, he has three sons, and there are other houses around.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So that is not a single house sitting in an open area?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: The shells that landed on Dalip Murati's house, did they cause any damage?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: You mean from the mortar fire? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And did these shells cause any injuries?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes. As a result, Dalip Murati was killed. The house was burned, the cattle and everything else that was in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And on this morning, on the 12th, were other shells being fired and landing in other parts of the village, in and around the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: From which part do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: From any location, are you aware of any other shelling going on in and around the village of Ljuboten, on the morning of the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: But who was shelling? What do you mean, and in what direction?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: My question is: Regardless of where shelling was coming from, did you hear any other shells landing in and around the village? Is there any other shells whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes, there were many.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. And you were also asked several questions about NLA activity and recruitment in Ljuboten, and I believe this was on page 33 of the transcript. You testified that, as a 14-year-old in 2001, you did not interested in the activities of the NLA. At this time, did you have any personal knowledge of which villagers, if any, were in the NLA?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, I didn't. As every army that has its own secrets, maybe this army, too, had its secrets that were not open for every child or ordinary person.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, at this time, I would like to call up Mr. Murati's statement, which I believe is exhibit P405. And if we can go to -- it's page 3 in the English version, paragraph 11, I'm particularly interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, I'm going to read to you part of paragraph 11, and perhaps you could follow along by reading the Albanian version at the same time. I will start from the third line, the third sentence. "Being asked to elaborate what I understand about army and police, I say that I have seen police reservists in army uniforms, which means camouflage uniforms. Being asked, I can't say I have seen any patches. I say that I was too far away for that. Some of these people were also wearing black T-shirts. Some of them were wearing masks. Being asked for the police, I say these people were wearing blue police uniforms." So, Mr. Murati, were you able to follow that in the Albanian version of your statement?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So, here, are you drawing a distinction between regular police and reservist police?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Yes. The regular police was wearing blue uniforms, while the reservists and the army had another type of uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. And you described the reservists as sometimes wearing camouflage pants with black T-shirts. Could you describe the army uniform?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Upper part was black T-shirts; and lower part, army trousers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, just to clarify this point, are you talking here about police reservists, or are you talking about members of the Macedonian army?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt -- sorry to interrupt, Your Honour, but the question was just answered. He was asked about the army uniform and he described them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm not clear, Mr. Dobbyn, what direction you were headed in.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the -- there is some description of the uniform. I'm trying to clarify exactly what the Macedonian police were wearing, as opposed to army members. There may have been some, perhaps, translation or at least just a misunderstanding on this part. I just want to clarify, to make sure what description we are getting of what uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So, Mr. Murati, could you describe -- I'm sorry. We will take this back a step. Can you please describe what members of the police reservists would wear?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: Same as the army members.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Did they have different insignia? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I already said that I didn't see any insignia, any patch with anything written on it. I only spoke about the uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: In the past, before or even after the events of 10 to 12 August, 2001, had you ever had the opportunity --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise to my colleague, but I will object. This does not arise out of the cross-examination; and, further more, it will have no relevance to the testimony of this witness, since he has clearly indicated on a number of occasion that he saw no patches or insignia on that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: On your first point, I'm afraid I disagree. This issue was raised in cross-examination, but I really think are you on a barren patch Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I will move on then, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honour -- sorry --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, you were asked some questions regarding your statement that you believe the police had avoided the open ground below your house, and you responded to the questioning that you believe they may have assumed that someone would shoot at them, and that's why you believed they would have avoided this area. Can I just ask you, Mr. Murati, did you see, at any time, anyone from the village shooting at the police as they moved through the village?

utterances.speaker: SEDAT MURATI
utterances.text: No, I didn't. There was no shooting by the villagers. Nobody was armed. Everybody was minding his/her own business. They were workers, simple workers, not interested in war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Murati, you will be pleased to know that that concludes the questions that will be asked of you. The Chamber would thank you for coming to The Hague and for the assistance that you have been able to give. And you are now, of course, able to leave and return to your normal activities, and the court officer will show you out. Thank you, again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. It was my pleasure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, I understand there is a matter that you wish to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are two procedural matters which, if I may, I would like to raise. The first is a document which is marked for identification as Prosecution Exhibit P382. It was marked for identification on the 19th of July during the testimony of General Galevski at page 3834 of the transcript. This is the collective agreement or joint staff agreement of the Ministry of Interior. It was also discussed at length during cross-examination with Mr. Galevski on the 17th of July. When the Prosecution asked that it be marked for identification rather than tendered, it was because at that time the full Macedonian version was not available on e-court. That problem has now been corrected and is well -- there is a better English translation of the number of the articles that are contained in this document. So, at this time, the Prosecution would move for the admission of P382.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document marked for identification as P382 will become Exhibit P382.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And the last point is: I hope that the Chamber will recall that at some point, it was probably in mid to late June, that the Prosecution informed the Chamber that the parties had discussed the so-called court files from Basic Court II, which are exhibits P46 through P55. And, although, that is only about 11 so-called P numbers, exhibit numbers, those files actually contain multiple documents. And the Prosecution and the Defence are in agreement, in coordination with Ms. Guduric, our court officer, that it would be much easier, actually, for all concerned, if on e-court those numbers are actually -- excuse me, those exhibits are actually broken down and given an individual number; so, for example, we would have 46.1, 46.2, et cetera. The Prosecution has provided a spreadsheet to the Defence which would describe how this would work. The Defence are in agreement with this initiative, and we simply seek the Chamber's approval before providing more formal memo and request to Ms. Guduric to actually begin this process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The idea seems very sensible and will make it easier for all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there any other matter? Well, we're finishing about 20 minutes earlier but the witness is finished. So we resume on Monday at, I believe, 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 27th day of August, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.23 p.m.,
